findings: The earlier insertion has a top spectral-tilt boundary error of 0.29 seconds; the fade-through-silence insertion has 0.14 seconds. Both proposals arrive after the inserted interval.

The later insertion yields no confirmed new mapping and no proposal. One post-edit cue is rejected for unsupported timing and then low beginning confidence; only the following cue produces an accepted new offset anchor. The failure is retained.
The continuous paired-gain control keeps one region, no gap or boundary proposal, and 0.205-second constant-offset tracking p95. One negative control does not calibrate specificity.
All three inserted-scene assessments fail the unchanged full-scene gates. A correct eventual boundary proposal is not first-playback recovery.

The late insertion exits the generic probe successfully because that probe scores a constant -100-second oracle. Its separate scene oracle correctly reports no recovery and 30.220-second p95; the generic passed flag is not scene acceptance.
nextAction: Improve post-edit temporal-anchor availability under the unchanged text/timing confidence requirements before relying on a boundary proposal. Keep early causal absence detection and delayed boundary learning as separate unresolved requirements.
